new_statements.translation: (2) Tones 2 (21) and 3 (31) are close in pitch value and contour. Tones 4 (23) and 5 (45) are often pronounced as mid-level 33 and high-level 55 in connected speech, and so are the corresponding checked tones 7a and 8b. […] (5) There is tone change: in disyllabic words the first syllable changes [tone] and the second does not; this is probably connected with the 'light-before, heavy-after' syllable-rhythm characteristic of Chadong. E.g. tin4(1) kwa1 'thigh', lən3(1) ti 'child' (base tone in parentheses).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Chadong is an eight-tone language (tones 1-8 = 53, 21, 31, 23, 45, 35, 5/31, 23 per Li Rulong et al. 2012 as reported on zh-Wikipedia). The only prominence statement found: disyllabic words have a 'front-light, back-heavy' (前轻后重, i.e. weak-strong / iambic) syllable rhythm; the first (light) syllable undergoes tone change while the second (heavy) syllable keeps its base tone. In effect the final syllable of a disyllabic word is the prominent one; no independent word-stress rule beyond this rhythmic remark is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated in the retrieved text; the statement is hedged ('大概', 'probably'). Remark (2) notes tones 4 (23) and 5 (45) and checked tones 7a/8b often level out to 33/55 in connected speech.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: disyllabic words (lexical items cited in isolation, e.g. 'thigh', 'child'); remark (2) concerns connected speech (语流). Variety described: Chadong of 思吉村 Siji village, 茶洞乡 Chadong township, 临桂县 Lingui county; author states internal geographic variation is minor and does not form dialects.
new_statements.identity_note: Same languoid (chad1240 / cdy). Li Jinfang's description is explicitly of the 思吉村 Siji village variety of Chadong township, Lingui county, Guangxi (本节介绍思吉村茶洞语); he states Chadong has minor geographic variation not amounting to dialects, with southern villages and Liangjiang town showing Pinghua/Mandarin/Zhuang contact effects. Li Rulong et al. 2012 may describe a different village point.
